extracted.intended_audience: National Capital Planning Commission staff (PAO/SAOP/CIO), contract managers, privacy officers, and individuals making Privacy Act requests
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and requirements for NCPC handling of Systems of Records under the Privacy Act, including notice, SORN content, safeguards, disclosure conditions, request/appeal procedures, fees, and Privacy Impact Assessments. Covers agency responsibilities, employee conduct, contractor obligations, and individual request processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for relying on third-party information
rubrics_metrics.description: The NCPC shall consider the following when deciding whether information can be obtained from a third party or an Individual:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Whether the information sought can only be obtained from a third party; (2) Whether the cost to collect the information from an Individual is unreasonable compared to the cost of collecting the information from a third party; (3) Whether there is a risk of collecting inaccurate information from a third party that could result in a determination adverse to the Individual concerned; (4) Whether the information collected requires verification by a third party; and (5) Whether the Individual can verify information collected from third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on maintaining records of First Amendment activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The NCPC shall not Maintain Records describing how an Individual exercises rights guaranteed by the First Amendment unless expressly authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records describing First Amendment activity may be Maintained only if (a) expressly authorized by statute, (b) authorized by the Individual about whom the Record is Maintained, or (c) pertinent to and within the scope of an authorized law enforcement activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to Individuals supplying information (minimum content and form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Individual asked to supply information about himself/herself to be added to a System of Records shall be informed by the NCPC of the basis for requesting the information, its potential use, and the consequences of not supplying the information. Notice shall state at a minimum specified items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum content (§603.5(a)): (1) The legal authority for NCPC’s solicitation and whether disclosure is mandatory or voluntary; (2) The principal purpose(s) for which NCPC intends to use the information; (3) The potential routine uses as published in a SORN; (4) The effects upon the individual, if any, of not providing all or any part of the requested Information. Form and delivery (§603.5(b)-(c)): When collecting on a standard form, notice shall be on the form, a tear-off sheet, or a separate form as practical. NCPC may ask an Individual to acknowledge in writing receipt of the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: SORN publication timing and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: The NCPC shall publish a notice in the Federal Register describing each System of Records 40-days prior to establishment or revision; the SORN must include specified elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SORN must include (§603.6(b)): (1) Name and location of the System (name to identify general purpose; location to indicate main server/central files and physical address); (2) Categories/types of Individuals on whom NCPC Maintains Records; (3) Categories/types of Records in the System; (4) Statutory or Executive Order authority for Maintenance; (5) Purpose(s)/explanation for collecting the Records, including identification of all internal and routine uses; (6) Policies/practices regarding storage, retrieval, access controls, retention and disposal; (7) Title and business address of agency official responsible; (8) Procedures for notification to an Individual who requests whether a System contains a Record about them; (9) Sources of Records in the System.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and minimum safeguards to protect Records
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall implement administrative, technical and physical safeguards to protect security and confidentiality of Records and guard against anticipated threats/hazards that could cause substantial harm, embarrassment, inconvenience, or unfairness to Individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual Records (§603.7(b)) minimum safeguards: (1) Post warning signs limiting access to authorized persons and advising of criminal penalties for unauthorized disclosure; (2) During work hours, restrict occupancy to authorized persons or store Records in locked containers/rooms; (3) During non-working hours, store Records in locked storage container and room; (4) Locks used shall not be disengageable with a master key that opens other rooms. Computerized Records (§603.7(c)): maintained at minimum subject to safeguards recommended by NIST SP 800–53 or any superseding NIST/federal guidance. Also maintain OPM personnel Records per 5 CFR 293.106–293.107 (§603.7(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee conduct regarding Records
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees with duties requiring access to and handling of Records shall protect integrity, security, and confidentiality; disclosure, alteration, or destruction permitted only under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees must at all times protect Records (§603.8(a)). Disclosure prohibited unless permitted by §603.10(b), by part 602, or disclosed to the Individual to whom the Record pertains (§603.8(b)). Alteration/destruction allowed only in course of regular duties or as allowed by NARA regulations or required by a court; Records shall not be destroyed/disposed of while subject to a pending request, appeal, or lawsuit under the Privacy Act (§603.8(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract requirements for third-party operated Systems of Records
rubrics_metrics.description: When a contract provides for third-party operation of a SOR on behalf of the NCPC, the contract must require application of the Privacy Act and NCPC rules and designate oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contract shall require that the requirements of the Privacy Act and the rules in this part be applied to such System (§603.9(a)). The Division Director responsible shall designate an NCPC employee to oversee and manage the SOR operated by the contractor (§603.9(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for disclosure and enumerated exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally no Record contained in a SOR shall be disclosed by any means to any person or another agency unless prior written consent is obtained from the Individual, except as provided by enumerated exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure exceptions (§603.10(b)) include: (1) To NCPC employees for performance of duties; (2) Required by FOIA; (3) For a Routine Use as described in a SORN; (4) To Bureau of Census for statistical purposes in non-identifiable form; (5) To an Individual providing written assurance for research/statistical use in non-identifiable form; (6) To NARA for records warranting permanent retention; (7) To a law enforcement agency for civil/criminal activity with a written request specifying Record(s) and purpose; (8) To any person upon demonstration of compelling information that an Individual’s health or safety is at stake (with notification to the Individual at last known address upon disclosure); (9) To either House of Congress and committees for Records within their jurisdiction; (10) To the Comptroller General or authorized representatives; (11) Pursuant to a court order; (12) To a consumer reporting agency collecting a government claim as authorized by 31 U.S.C. 3711(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting of disclosures and retention of accountings
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for disclosures to NCPC employees for duties and FOIA-required disclosures, NCPC shall prepare an accounting when a Record is disclosed and maintain accountings for a minimum period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounting shall record the date, nature, and purpose of the disclosure and the name and address of the person or agency to whom disclosure was made (§603.11(a)). Maintain accountings for a minimum of five years or the life of the Record, whichever is greater. Except for disclosures under §603.10(b)(7) (law enforcement), accountings shall be made available to the Individual on request (§603.11(b)). If a Record is amended or corrected after an accounting was made, the Individual and/or agency originally disclosed to shall be informed (§603.11(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for requests to determine existence of Records
rubrics_metrics.description: An Individual seeking to determine whether a System of Records contains Records pertaining to them shall appear in person or submit written correspondence to NCPC’s PAO with specified content and follow timing rules for response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests: in-person by appointment at NCPC official place of business or by written correspondence to the PAO; written requests via mail/email/facsimile directed to addresses on NCPC website; the words 'Privacy Act Request' should appear prominently (§603.12(a)). The Request shall state seeking information concerning existence of Records and supply information describing the System as set forth in a SORN (§603.12(b)). PAO shall notify Requester in writing within 20 Workdays whether a System contains Records unless Records were compiled in reasonable anticipation of civil action or are OPM employee Records, in which case Request is denied. Denial must state reason and advise right to appeal within 60 days per §603.16 (§603.12(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for access requests (content, identification, fees, timelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Individual seeking access to Records about themselves shall apply in person or in writing to the PAO and meet specified content, identification, fee-willingness, and timeline requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request content (§603.13(b)): (1) State Request is made pursuant to the Privacy Act; (2) Describe requested Records in sufficient detail including dates and System name/ID as in SORNs; (3) State willingness to pay fees per §603.17 or maximum fee willing to pay. Identification (§603.13(c)): in-person requesters present valid photographic ID; mail requesters must state full name, address, date of birth, sign the request and either notarize or include a declaration under penalty of perjury. PAO shall determine within 20 Workdays whether to grant or deny access and notify in writing with reasons; denials for OPM jurisdiction must advise Requester to contact OPM and advise right to appeal (§603.13(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for amendment or correction of Records
rubrics_metrics.description: An Individual seeking to amend or correct a Record they believe inaccurate, irrelevant, untimely or incomplete shall submit a written request to the PAO meeting specified content and procedural prerequisites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request content (§603.14(b)): (1) State the request is made pursuant to the Privacy Act; (2) Describe the Record sufficiently including dates and System name/ID; (3) State in detail reasons why the Record or portions are not accurate, relevant, timely or complete; (4) Include copies of supporting documents; (5) State specifically the changes sought and propose specific language for rewriting or additions. Prerequisite (§603.14(c)): requester must previously have requested and been granted access and inspected or been given a copy of the Record. PAO decision within 20 Workdays; if request fails to meet requirements, PAO advises deficiency and tolls the timeframe until additional information received; failure to provide additional information in reasonable time results in rejection (§603.14(d)). PAO’s decision must be in writing stating basis; if approved, ensure amendment/correction; if denied, place a notation of dispute and, if accountings were made, advise previous recipients that an amendment/correction or notation has been made (§603.14(e)-(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for requests for accounting of Record disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: An Individual seeking information regarding an accounting of disclosure of a Record shall submit a written request to the PAO with specified content; NCPC shall respond within a set timeframe and include disclosure details if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request (§603.15(a)-(b)): state request is pursuant to the Privacy Act and describe the requested Record in sufficient detail to determine whether it is contained in an accounting. PAO shall notify the Requester within 20 Workdays and advise if the Record was included in an accounting; if so, response shall include date, nature and purpose of disclosure and name/address of person or agency to whom disclosure was made. Denials due to OPM jurisdiction must advise Requester to contact OPM; advise right to appeal in event of Adverse Determination (§603.15(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals of Adverse Determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals must appeal Adverse Determinations in writing to the Chairman within 30 Workdays with specified content; the Chairman will respond within 20 Workdays and the appeal process and judicial review rights are defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal content (§603.16(a)-(b)): appeals (except those under paragraph (d)) addressed to the Chairman, words 'Privacy Act Request' prominent; made within 30 Workdays of decision; include statement of legal/factual basis for objection, daytime phone or email for contact, copies of initial request and PAO response, and for fee-waiver adverse determinations demonstrate compliance with part 602. Chairman shall respond in writing within 20 WorkDays; if appeal granted, NCPC acts promptly after receipt of any required fees; if denied, letter states reasons, that decision is final, and advises right to seek judicial review in specified District Courts. Appeals based on OPM jurisdiction go to OPM per 5 CFR 297.306. NCPC will not act on appeal if underlying request becomes subject of litigation; must exhaust administrative appeal before seeking court review (§603.16(c)-(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for duplication, search, and review
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall charge duplication fees under part 602; special rules apply for inspection and for search/review fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPC shall charge for duplication of Records per fee schedule in part 602 (§603.17(a)). NCPC shall not charge duplication fees when the Requester inspects Records personally but copies may be provided at agency discretion (§603.17(a)). NCPC shall not charge any fees for search for or review of Records requested by an Individual (§603.17(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) requirements and content
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall conduct a PIA consistent with the E-Government Act and OMB Memo M–03–22 before certain IT systems or new IT-based collections that collect IIF; the PIA must be prepared by designated personnel, include specified analyses, identify choices made, be verified and approved, and be posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIA triggers (§603.18(a)): before developing/procuring IT systems or projects that collect/maintain/disseminate Information in Identifiable Form (IIF); or installing a new collection using IT that includes IIF for 10 or more persons. Preparation (§603.18(b)): coordinated effort of privacy Officers (SAOP, PAO), Division Directors, CIO, and IT staff. Content (§603.18(c)): shall analyze and describe (1) information to be collected; (2) reason the information is being collected; (3) intended use; (4) identity of those with whom information will be shared; (5) opportunities Individuals have to decline or consent and how to consent; (6) manner in which information will be secured; (7) extent to which the system is being created under the Privacy Act. PIA must also identify choices NCPC made regarding the IT system/collection as a result of preparing the PIA (§603.18(d)). CCB shall verify a PIA has been prepared before approving IT procure/development (§603.18(e)). Approval/signature (§603.18(f)): SAOP shall approve and sign the PIA (or Executive Director if SAOP is Contracting Officer). Following approval, NCPC shall post the PIA on its website (§603.18(g)).
